title: The insect body plan
keyIdea: Every insect has the same body plan: three body parts called the head, the thorax and the abdomen, and exactly six legs. All six legs join the thorax, the middle part. The antennae and eyes are on the head, and the wings, when an insect has them, also join the thorax. Insects have no bones inside. Their skeleton is a hard case on the outside, called an exoskeleton, so a young insect must moult (shed the old case) to grow bigger. Counting legs and body parts tells you if a minibeast is an insect: a spider has 8 legs and 2 parts, so it is not.
familyTip: Go on a bug hunt with a hand lens. For each minibeast you find, count the legs and the body parts together before you say if it is an insect. Look for a shed case on a plant stem or under a leaf in summer.

visual.caption: Which body part does each one belong to? Drag each card to a box, or tap the card and then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: name the three body parts, attach six legs, place antennae, eyes and wings, help a young insect moult, and sort minibeasts.

kid: An insect has three body parts. The head is at the front. The thorax is in the middle. The abdomen is the big part at the back.
Every insect has six legs. All six join the thorax. None grow on the head or the abdomen.
The head has the eyes and two antennae. Insects feel and smell with their antennae. Most insects have wings, and the wings join the thorax too.
Insects have no bones inside. A hard case on the outside holds them up. It is called an exoskeleton. It cannot stretch, so a young insect sheds it to grow. This is called moulting.
adult: Ages 7 to 9. In England, Year 3 and Year 4 science asks children to compare animals by their body parts and to group living things. NGSS 4-LS1-1 asks how body structures help an animal survive. Insects are the classic first group defined by structure. Every insect has three body parts (head, thorax, abdomen) and six jointed legs on the thorax. It has one pair of antennae on the head. Most adults have one or two pairs of wings, also on the thorax.

Insects are arthropods. They have no bones; their skeleton is a hard outer case called an exoskeleton. The case cannot stretch, so a young insect sheds it several times as it grows. This is moulting. The new case is soft at first, swells, then hardens. Most adult insects stop moulting.

Common mistakes: putting legs on the abdomen because it is the biggest part. Thinking every minibeast or bug is an insect: spiders have 8 legs and 2 body parts, and woodlice have 14 legs. Thinking a worker ant is not an insect because it has no wings. Thinking insects have bones that grow. In the lab a leg will not fit the wrong part, a card will not sort and the case will not stretch.

practice.prompt: Which body part do an insect's six legs join?
practice.hint: Think of the middle part of the insect, between the head and the back part.
practice.explain: All six legs join the thorax, the middle part. The abdomen is bigger, but no legs join it.

practice.prompt: There are {n} beetles on a log. How many legs do they have altogether?
practice.hint: Every insect has exactly 6 legs. Count 6 for each beetle.
practice.explain: A beetle is an insect, so it has 6 legs: {n} × 6 = {=6*n} legs.

practice.prompt: {n} ants walk past. How many body parts do they have altogether?
practice.hint: Each insect has 3 body parts: head, thorax and abdomen.
practice.explain: Each ant has 3 body parts, so {n} ants have {n} × 3 = {=3*n} body parts.

practice.prompt: A minibeast has 8 legs and 2 body parts. What is it?
choices: Not an insect, it could be a spider
practice.hint: Count again. How many legs does every insect have?
practice.explain: Insects have 6 legs and 3 body parts. 8 legs and 2 parts is a spider, which is not an insect.

practice.hint: The antennae are used to feel and smell. Which part leads the way?
practice.explain: The two antennae grow on the head, next to the eyes. The thorax has the legs and wings.

pool.prompt: What are the three body parts of an insect, from front to back?
pool.hint: The middle part is where the legs join. Which word names it?
pool.explain: Head at the front, thorax in the middle, abdomen at the back.

pool.prompt: A woodlouse has 14 legs. Is it an insect?
choices: Yes, because it has a hard shell
pool.hint: Count the legs. Being small, or having a hard case, is not the test.
pool.explain: A woodlouse has 14 legs, so it is not an insect. It is a crustacean, a cousin of crabs.

pool.prompt: How does a young grasshopper grow bigger?
choices: It moults its hard case and grows a new one
pool.hint: Insects have their skeleton on the outside. Can a hard case stretch?
pool.explain: The exoskeleton cannot stretch, so the grasshopper sheds it (moults). The new soft case stretches, then hardens.

pool.prompt: A worker ant has no wings. Is it an insect?
pool.hint: Most insects have wings, but what is the real test?
pool.explain: Some insects have no wings. An ant has 6 legs and 3 body parts, so it is an insect.

pool.prompt: A spider has 8 legs and an insect has 6. How many legs do {n} spiders have altogether?
pool.hint: Spiders are not insects. Count 8 legs for each spider.
pool.explain: Each spider has 8 legs, so {n} spiders have {n} × 8 = {=8*n} legs.

pool.prompt: A butterfly has two pairs of wings. How many wings do {n} butterflies have altogether?
pool.hint: Two pairs is 2 + 2 = 4 wings for each butterfly.
pool.explain: Each butterfly has 4 wings, so {n} butterflies have {n} × 4 = {=4*n} wings.

pool.prompt: Which part of an insect do the wings join?
pool.hint: The wings join the same part as the legs.
pool.explain: The wings join the thorax, the same part as the legs. Muscles inside the thorax move them.

choices: A hard case on the outside of the body
pool.hint: Exo means outside. Where is an insect's hard part?
pool.explain: An exoskeleton is a skeleton on the outside: a hard case that holds the insect up and keeps it safe.

pool.prompt: Ben says legs join the abdomen because it is the biggest part. What is wrong?
choices: Legs join the thorax, the middle part
pool.hint: Size is not the clue. Which part are all six legs fixed to?
pool.explain: The abdomen is the biggest part, but it has no legs. All six legs join the thorax.
